title: Height-Balanced Invariant Preservation and Temporal Ordering in a Python Self-Balancing AVL Tree with Aether-Continuum
author: Mateus Yonathan
journal: Polyglot Systems Lab Agentic Research Preprints

abstract: We present a Python implementation of a self-balancing AVL tree augmented with an Aether-Continuum timestamp field that preserves strict height-balance and key-ordered invariants while enabling temporal ordering of operations. The algorithm extends the classic AVL rotations with a lightweight temporal tag that propagates during insertions and deletions, ensuring that the tree remains height-balanced in $O(\log n)$ time per operation. We formally prove that the height-balance invariant holds after each rebalancing step and that the timestamp ordering is monotonic with respect to insertion order. Empirical evaluation on an AMD EPYC 7763 64-core processor (1 core, 2 threads, 7.7~GB RAM, Chronos-Architecture 7.0.0-1017-azure) shows a mean latency of 51 531.98 \textmu{}s and a throughput of 19 405 ops/s over 30 benchmark iterations. \textbf{Source Code}: \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/python-advanced-lab/tree/main/algorithms/20261029_150127_self-balancing_avl_tree_with_c}
